results.title: Rupiah weakens and IHSG falls 1.69% as PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) and PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) record the largest transaction values
results.body: The Indonesian rupiah weakened 0.21% to IDR 17,884 per US dollar and the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 1.69% to 6,277.04 on Tuesday. Trading volume reached Rp14.45 trillion across 33.71 billion shares, with PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) and PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) recording the largest transaction values of Rp875.45 billion and Rp714.09 billion respectively, while BUMI’s share price fell 3.64% and also fell 4.17% as reported. All sector indices slipped, led by energy down 2.76% and consumer‑cyclical up only 0.33%, and the IHSG broke below its 100‑day and 60‑day moving averages, potentially testing the psychological 6,200 level. Analysts noted that investors await the Bank Indonesia board meeting, with consensus expecting the BI Rate to stay at 5.75%, and the IHSG was the worst‑performing emerging‑market index in the Asia‑Pacific region that day.

results.title: Nickel stocks pressured by RKAB approval uncertainty and HPM regulation, PT PAM Mineral Tbk (NICL) leads declines.
results.body: The article reports that nickel stocks are under pressure due to uncertainty over RKAB approval and changes to the Harga Patokan Mineral (HPM) regulation, compounded by oversupply and stagnant global nickel prices. Year‑to‑date performance shows PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO) down 11.70%, PT Trimegah Bangun Persada Tbk (NCKL) down 21.46%, PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) down 18.55%, PT Central Omega Resources Tbk (DKFT) down 14.84%, PT PAM Mineral Tbk (NICL) down 64.61%, and PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) down 1.25%. The analyst notes that integrated issuers such as PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) and PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO) have relatively stronger resilience because of diversified portfolios and healthy capital structures. Outlook for 2027 is cautiously optimistic, contingent on smoother RKAB licensing, cost‑efficiency gains, and potential demand recovery from electric‑vehicle batteries and stainless‑steel markets.

results.title: IHSG drops over 1% as PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) drags the index
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 84.62 points, or 1.33%, to 6,300.11 on 22 September 2026, extending the decline from the previous session. The drop was led by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), which alone pulled the index down 14.6 points, followed by PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN) (-7.74 points), PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS) (-2.98 points), PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM) (-2.77 points), PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) (-2.45 points), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) (-2.21 points), PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) (-2.21 points), PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) (-2.15 points), PT Impack Pratama Industri Tbk (IMPC) (-2.11 points) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) (-1.98 points). In contrast, PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) added the most positive impact with +2.11 points, while PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) and PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) contributed +0.38 and +0.36 points respectively. Broad sector weakness saw energy, utilities and property lead the red zone, and the market remained sensitive to domestic uncertainty over the upcoming Bank Indonesia rate decision and global oil price and geopolitical tensions.

results.title: Foreign investors net sold Rp 510.07 bn of Indonesian stocks, led by PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI)
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 510.07 bn on Monday, sending the Indonesia Composite Index (IHSG) down 0.88% to 6,384.72 points. The ten stocks with the largest foreign net outflows were PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) (Rp 140.61 bn), PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) (Rp 139.93 bn), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) (Rp 131.34 bn), PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) (Rp 114.62 bn), PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) (Rp 32.42 bn), PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) (Rp 26.38 bn), PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (CPIN) (Rp 25.81 bn), PT Alamtri Resoruces Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) (Rp 22.32 bn), PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) (Rp 21.98 bn), and PT Energi Mega Persada Tbk (ENRG) (Rp 16.65 bn). Overall market activity was high, with 26.78 billion shares traded for a total value of Rp 11.77 trillion. Sectorally, infrastructure fell 1.38% while transport rose 0.55%, health gained 0.21% and property remained flat.

results.title: PT Adhi Karya Tbk (ADHI) signs Master Restructuring Agreement for Rp 3 trillion debt
results.body: PT Adhi Karya Tbk (ADHI) signed a Master Restructuring Agreement (MRA) on 18 September 2026 to restructure its total debt of approximately Rp 3 trillion. The agreement is with the creditor banks PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI), with BMRI also serving as the facility agent. Under the MRA, Tranche A provides a term loan of Rp 1,546,885,366,367 with a 15‑year balloon payment and a 3.5 % annual interest (1 % cash quarterly and 2.5 % deferred to 2041); Tranche B supplies a term loan of Rp 1,455,728,987,624 with a 5‑year bullet payment, a 1 % annual interest paid quarterly and funded by ADHI’s divestments; Tranche C covers interest‑free profit‑sharing accrued from the stand‑still period and will be repaid in equal installments over 18 months from the effective date. The restructuring aims to preserve ADHI’s business continuity, improve its operational and financial performance, and enable full repayment of its obligations to the creditor banks.

results.title: PT Adhi Karya (Persero) Tbk (ADHI) signs Master Restructuring Agreement to restructure Rp3 trillion of debt
results.body: PT Adhi Karya (Persero) Tbk (ADHI) signed a Master Restructuring Agreement (MRA) on 18 September 2026 to restructure its Rp3 trillion debt. The agreement, reached with creditor banks PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) (BMRI) Tbk, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) (BBRI) Tbk and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) (BBNI) Tbk, splits the debt into three tranches: Tranche A of Rp1.55 trillion with 3.5% annual interest (1% cash quarterly, 2.5% deferred to 2041), Tranche B of Rp1.46 trillion with 1% annual interest payable quarterly over five years, and Tranche C covering interest or profit‑sharing payable in interest‑free installments over 18 months. The MRA becomes effective after shareholder approval at the upcoming RUPS and fulfillment of the agreement’s conditions, as noted by President Director Moeharmein Zein Chaniago. ADHI will refocus on its core engineering and construction business, streamline its organization and portfolio, and aim to improve operational efficiency and financial management.

results.title: Foreign outflow hits Rp1.79 trillion, with BBCA and BMRI leading net sells
results.body: On 18 September 2024, foreign investors recorded a net outflow of Rp1.78 trillion on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, with foreign buying rising to Rp7.04 trillion and selling to Rp8.81 trillion. The largest net‑sell positions were posted by PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) with Rp222.05 billion (35.43 million shares) and PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) with Rp108.93 billion (25.45 million shares), followed by PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM), PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI). The top net‑buy positions were held by PT Aneka Tambang (Persero) Tbk (ANTM) at Rp41.09 billion (12.49 million shares), PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) at Rp22.40 billion (4.55 million shares), PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) at Rp15.59 billion (1.27 million shares), PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) at Rp12.47 billion (4.28 million shares) and PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) at Rp10.48 billion (19.88 million shares). These figures show the breadth of foreign trading activity across major banks, telecom, mining and battery‑materials stocks.

results.title: IHSG Opens Weaker at Start of Week, Pressured by Global Sentiment
results.body: The IHSG opened 1.36% lower at 6,452 on Monday as rising oil prices above $100 per barrel and an 85% probability of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting pressured sentiment. Foreign investors sold a net Rp2.31 trillion in the regular market, while trading volume reached 6.53 billion shares worth Rp3.06 trillion. Technical indicators show a hammer pattern at the 6,475-6,375 support zone with the index holding above its 20-day moving average at 6,533, suggesting a potential rebound. Brokerages offered divergent outlooks: BRI Danareksa sees a constructive bias targeting resistance at 6,600-6,700 and favors UNTR, IMPC, and TINS; Phintraco expects sideways movement between 6,450-6,700 and picks ANTM, ASII, EMAS, MDKA, and ISAT; CGS International forecasts varied gains with support at 6,465-6,390 and resistance at 6,620-6,695, recommending TAPG, AALI, ISAT, TINS, AMMN, and EMAS; Panin Sekuritas anticipates further weakness due to geopolitical tensions and foreign outflows, selecting INET, BRMS, and INCO.

results.title: IDNFinancials weekly roundup highlights Djarum Group's planned control of Narasi media, the INRU export case, and Danantara's disputed Rp120 trillion state deposit
results.body: The weekly most-read articles on IDNFinancials.com for September 7-13, 2026 center on three major domestic stories: Djarum Group's move to control Narasi media founded by Najwa Shihab, the INRU export case implicating Djarum as a suspect, and controversy over Danantara's Rp120 trillion deposit to the state treasury ordered by President Prabowo Subianto. Other top corporate stories include Bank Mandiri (BMRI) issuing US$750 million dollar bonds at a 7.35% coupon, Bumi Resources (BUMI) acquiring 100% of Loyal Metals, and Morgan Stanley increasing its stake in GoTo Gojek Tokopedia (GOTO) while shares trade at Rp50. President Prabowo's mandate for universal bank account ownership assigns roles to Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI) and Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI), while the Whoosh high-speed rail project undergoes an 80-year debt restructuring.

results.title: Grup Djarum, Low Tuck Kwong, and Prajogo Pangestu Stocks Weigh Down the IHSG for the Week
results.body: During the week of 7–11 September 2026, shares of PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bayan Resources Tbk, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk, PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk, PT Barito Pacific Tbk, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, PT Barito Renewables Energy Tbk, and PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk fell sharply, delivering the largest negative contributions to the IHSG, with BBCA down 5.60% (‑33.09 points), BYAN down 10.51% (‑23.63 points), BBRI down 3.54% (‑17.51 points), DSSA down 6.78% (‑6.86 points), BBNI down 4.82% (‑6.26 points), BRMS down 5.59% (‑5.95 points), BRPT down 5.03% (‑5.22 points), BMRI down 1.36% (‑4.90 points), BREN down 3.57% (‑4.64 points), and VKTR down 8.09% (‑4.31 points). The composite index slipped 1.43% to 6,541,377, while total market capitalization fell 1.32% to Rp11,446 trillion and average daily transaction value dropped 14.88% to Rp16.36 trillion. Foreign investors posted a net sell of Rp690.19 billion on 11 September, contributing to a year‑to‑date net outflow of Rp71,415 trillion.

results.title: Mirae Asset Sekuritas assesses global pressures still weighing on the market
results.body: Mirae Asset Sekuritas says global sentiment continues to weigh on Indonesia’s market, noting that the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 1.33% to 6,589 amid a net foreign outflow of Rp748 billion. The pressure was most evident on banking stocks BBCA and BBRI, while foreign investors accumulated commodity‑linked shares such as ANTM, AADI, CUAN and PTBA. The firm cites macro factors including the US 10‑year Treasury yield near 5%, the ECB rate at 2.5%, high oil prices, the rupiah at roughly Rp17,547 per USD and a 10‑year SBN yield of 7.11% as limiting the transmission of global yields to the domestic market. Despite these headwinds, consumer confidence rose to 118.5 in August and Mirae Asset recommends a selective portfolio focused on strong fundamentals and solid cash flow.

results.title: PT Pembangunan Perumahan Tbk signs Master Restructuring Agreement to restructure Rp18.2 trillion debt with four state-owned banks
results.body: PT Pembangunan Perumahan Tbk signed a Master Restructuring Agreement on 10 September 2026 to restructure its Rp18.2 trillion debt with four state‑owned banks. The debt is divided into three tranches: Tranche A of about Rp13.33 trillion at 3.5% per year (1% cash quarterly and 2.5% deferred to 2041) to be repaid over 15 years via a balloon payment; Tranche B of about Rp4.05 trillion at 1% per year with a five‑year bullet payment funded by divestment proceeds; and Tranche C covering accrued interest from the standstill period, repaid in interest‑free installments over 18 months. The participating lenders are PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (acting as Facility Agent), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk and PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk. Certain working‑capital facilities tied to project owners are excluded from the restructuring and will be serviced independently of project cash flows.

results.title: PTPP Restructures Rp18.2 Trillion Debt, Detailing Payment Schemes
results.body: PT PP (Persero) Tbk (PTPP) has restructured Rp18.2 trillion of debt into three tranches: Tranche A (Rp13.33 trillion) with a 15‑year balloon payment and 3.5% interest, Tranche B (Rp4.05 trillion) with a five‑year bullet payment and 1% interest, and Tranche C covering interest or profit‑share accrued since the stand‑still, paid over 18 months. The restructuring, governed by a Master Restructuring Agreement signed on 10 September 2026 with PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, and PT Bank Syariah Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, will take effect after a shareholders’ meeting. PTPP aims to transform its business and finances to sustain operations, improve performance, and repay creditors. The agreement also excludes certain working‑capital facilities, which remain independent of project cash flows.

results.title: IHSG falls 0.58% in first session as foreign investors net sell Rp577 billion, led by PT Bank Central Asia Tbk and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) declined 0.58% to 6,647.50 in the first trading session on Wednesday (9/9), with total transaction value reaching Rp8.32 trillion. Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp577.21 billion, dominated by bank stocks with the largest market capitalization. PT Bank Central Asia Tbk posted the largest net foreign sell of Rp419.03 billion, followed by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk at Rp62.73 billion. Most sectoral indices weakened, with healthcare down 1.45% and technology down 1%, while transportation gained 2.15%. Regional Asian markets were mixed, with South Korea's KOSPI rising 1.01% and India's NIFTY falling 0.52%.

results.title: Bank Indonesia Flags Uneven Banking Liquidity, Highlights Tight Himbara LDR Driven by State-Led Credit Growth
results.body: Bank Indonesia Governor Destry Damayanti said banking liquidity distribution remains uneven despite M0 growing above 15% through August 2026, with the largest contributions coming from non-bank financial institutions and state-owned enterprises. The central bank highlighted that state-owned banks under Himbara face tighter liquidity, evidenced by loan-to-deposit ratios exceeding the industry average of 88.32% as of June 2026. Bank Mandiri recorded an LDR of 92.73%, Bank Rakyat Indonesia 91.3%, Bank Tabungan Negara 96.49%, and Bank Negara Indonesia 87.73%. Destry attributed the elevated Himbara LDRs to faster credit disbursement, particularly to the government ecosystem, with Bank Mandiri's lending to government and BUMNs surging 41.6% year-on-year to Rp 489 trillion and Bank Negara Indonesia's BUMN lending jumping 63.2% to Rp 197.8 trillion in the same period. The segmented liquidity reflects Indonesia's state-led intermediation model where growth is driven by government and BUMN borrowing including from Danantara.

results.title: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk Cut 2026 Net Interest Margin Targets Amid Liquidity Pressure
results.body: The article reports that PT Bank Mandiri Tbk and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk lowered their 2026 net interest margin (NIM) guidance as liquidity conditions tightened. PT Bank Mandiri Tbk reduced its NIM target range from 4.6‑4.8% to 4.5‑4.7% after its NIM fell 33 basis points and its cost of fund rose 12 basis points quarter‑on‑quarter, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk trimmed its range from 3.5‑3.8% to 3.3‑3.5% as its cost of fund increased 14 basis points. The other two big four banks, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk and PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, saw NIM decline of 20 and 10 basis points respectively but kept their original guidance, and the four banks collectively posted a 13% year‑on‑year rise in net profit to IDR 101.6 trillion, driven by PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (+24% yoy) and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (+17% yoy). Despite the margin pressure, credit growth remained robust at 12% yoy, provisioning trends varied with PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk raising provisions, and the banks’ stock prices moved modestly on the day, with PT Bank Mandiri Tbk up 1.15% and PT Bank Central Asia Tbk down 0.37%.

results.title: BRI (BBRI) Posts Rp 30.9 Trillion Net Profit for January-July 2026, Up 8% Year-on-Year
results.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) recorded a bank-only net profit of Rp 30.9 trillion for January through July 2026, representing an 8% year-on-year increase and reaching 53% of the 2026 consensus estimate. In July alone, net profit fell 12% year-on-year to Rp 3.4 trillion, driven by a 21% rise in provision expenses to Rp 3.6 trillion. Net interest income declined 2% year-on-year in July as funding costs rose 5%, compressing the net interest margin to 5.6% from 6.1% a year earlier. Credit costs improved to 3% from 3.8% in May, and the stock has gained about 8% over the past five trading sessions, with sustained micro-segment growth seen as critical for valuation recovery.

results.title: OJK revokes license of PT Bank Perekonomian Rakyat Syariah Gaido Indonesia, 13th bank closure in 2026
results.body: OJK has revoked the business license of PT Bank Perekonomian Rakyat Syariah Gaido Indonesia, marking the 13th bank closure in Indonesia in 2026. The revocation follows OJK’s earlier placement of the bank under BPR Syariah Dalam Penyehatan (BDP) on 15 August 2025 after the bank posted a KPMM ratio of negative 7.56% and a composite rating of PK‑5 for two consecutive periods (December 2024 and June 2025). On 13 August 2026 OJK upgraded supervision to BPR Syariah Dalam Resolusi (BDR), but the bank’s management and shareholders failed to meet the required capital and liquidity remediation, leading Lembaga Penjamin Simpanan (LPS) to decide on liquidation under Decision No 118/ADK3/2026. LPS will carry out the liquidation in accordance with Indonesian deposit‑insurance law after OJK formally cancelled the license on 1 September 2026.

results.title: OJK Revokes License of BPRS Gaido Indonesia, LPS Orders Liquidation
results.body: Indonesia's Financial Services Authority (OJK) revoked the operating license of PT Bank Perekonomian Rakyat Syariah Gaido Indonesia on 1 September 2026 after the sharia rural bank failed to meet capital requirements during a supervised recovery period. The bank had a minimum capital adequacy ratio (KPMM) of minus 7.56% and held the lowest composite health rating (PK-5) for two consecutive periods ending December 2024 and June 2025. Following the failed recovery, OJK placed the bank under resolution supervision (BDR) on 13 August 2026, and the Deposit Insurance Corporation (LPS) decided on 20 August 2026 to handle the bank through liquidation. LPS then requested the license revocation, which OJK executed, and LPS will now manage deposit insurance payouts and the liquidation process.

results.title: Investor.id popular news roundup covers BBRI dividend policy shift, gold jewelry prices, BI leadership transition, Chandra Asri Pacific acquisition expansion, and US Treasury bond buyback impact on gold
results.body: Investor.id's September 1, 2026 popular news roundup features five financial updates. PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk plans to gradually lower its dividend payout ratio from 92% in 2025 to 60% to prioritize capital strengthening, while Pluang Maju Sekuritas maintains a buy rating. Gold jewelry prices from retailers Raja Emas Indonesia, Hartadinata Abadi, and Laku Emas remained stable, and former Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo issued his first public statement since his July 25 resignation congratulating new Governor Destry Damayanti. PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk continues diversification through acquisitions including Aster Chemicals and Energy via a joint venture with Glencore, though Kiwoom advises wait-and-see, while Julius Baer notes the US Treasury's plan to double long-term bond buybacks from September may support gold prices.
